paragraphs: After the damaged cabinet and wet backing are removed, the floor and wall are checked for sound attachment points before the replacement is positioned. Measurements account for the cabinet width, countertop height, plumbing clearances and the finished floor thickness so the unit does not bind against adjacent components.

The cabinet is set level and plumb with shims where needed, then fastened into suitable wall framing. Filler strips and toe-kick panels are measured and cut to close the visible gaps without forcing the cabinet out of alignment.

paragraphs: Countertop, sink and plumbing reconnection are identified in the estimate because they may require separate trades. Once those interfaces are ready, doors and hardware are aligned, exposed edges are finished and the cabinet meets the retained run cleanly.

The installation does not cover unresolved leak repair or wet material behind the cabinet. Those conditions are addressed before the new unit is secured, preventing a replacement finish from hiding an active source or an unsound support surface.
